---
title: "stateMINT: the emulator"
---

stateMINT takes an EIR, the setting it belongs to, and the campaign under evaluation, and
returns prevalence and clinical-case trajectories over six years, three before the campaign and
three after. The EIR comes from [estiMINT](../04-estimint/index.qmd).

It emulates [`malariasimulation`](https://mrc-ide.github.io/malariasimulation/), which takes
minutes per scenario. Trained on a library of those runs, stateMINT reproduces their output in
milliseconds, so a fifty-scenario batch runs in under a second on a laptop CPU. Like any
emulator it is trustworthy only inside the range it was trained on.

The weights live on Hugging Face at
[`dide-ic/stateMINT`](https://huggingface.co/dide-ic/stateMINT), two checkpoints of about 38 MB,
one for prevalence and one for cases. The first call downloads and caches them.

## Inputs and outputs

The input is twelve scalars rather than a time series, describing the setting and the campaign.
The emulator reconstructs the time grid from them. The output is an array of shape `(B, 157)`,
one row per scenario and 157 fortnightly windows spanning day 2190 to day 4374, where the campaign
lands at day 3285, which puts three pre-campaign years at the front of every row and three response
years at the back.

Prevalence and cases are separately trained checkpoints, so asking for both means loading both and
calling each once. No single call returns the pair. Please see
[Running Scenarios](../06-scenarios/index.qmd) for a pipeline that does both.
